356.title: Divination Log
356.content:
Divination Practice: Flame reading, tea leaf reading, and smoke reading.
Practice 1: Predict tomorrow's weather with flame reading. The flame shot straight up. Sunny, I guess?
Practice 2: Check my fortune of the day with tea leaf reading. Seriously, which way is the right way to read it?
Practice 3: Foresee my practice partner's future with smoke reading. The smoke dispersed as soon as it rose. Does it mean... death?
...
Cyran told the divination professor that he didn't want to be my practice partner anymore. His reason? Every time I predicted his death, he never died, and that makes me a lousy diviner. How absurd!

Shouldn't he be happy he's alive? He could really use a new way of looking at things...

358.title: Stargazing Log 1
358.content:
I worked with Cyran to break down the Starshower spell, just like we planned. Honestly, I love talking about magic with him, even if he drives me crazy sometimes. It always sparks all these interesting ideas in my head.

That conversation got me thinking. Maybe I should start my observations with that constellation today. I really hope I catch something ancient again...

(Illegible observation log)

Cyran came along to stargaze with me, but... well, he's not exactly great at it. He didn't see anything.

He seemed kind of upset about it. Maybe I should plan a surprise to cheer him up next time?

Starshower made the night sky light up with a gorgeous meteor shower! That's honestly one of the reasons I love it so much!

Too bad my plan wasn't perfect. Cyran was excited at first, but when he figured out it was from Starshower, his mood changed. He said I shouldn't have wasted his time with such a "useless" spell.

It stung when he said that about my favorite spell. How could it be useless when it brings luck and joy to anyone who sees it?

Magic is supposed to make people happy, right? From that angle, Starshower might just be the most powerful spell in Esperia!

He just sneered when I said that. To him, magic's all about power, and anything like Starshower is just a fun trick with no real use.

Oh well, I guess we'll just have to agree to disagree.

Cyran came along to stargaze with me, but... well, he's not exactly great at it. He didn't see anything.

He seemed kind of upset about it. Maybe I should plan a surprise to cheer him up next time?

Starshower made the night sky light up with a gorgeous meteor shower! That's honestly one of the reasons I love it so much!

Too bad my plan wasn't perfect. Cyran was excited at first, but when he figured out it was from Starshower, his mood changed. He said I shouldn't have wasted his time with such a "useless" spell.

It stung when he said that about my favorite spell. How could it be useless when it brings luck and joy to anyone who sees it?

Magic is supposed to make people happy, right? From that angle, Starshower might just be the most powerful spell in Esperia!

He just sneered when I said that. To him, magic's all about power, and anything like Starshower is just a fun trick with no real use.

Oh well, I guess we'll just have to agree to disagree.

362.title: Rule Revisions
362.content:
Ah, yes, the <style="highlight">herbal tea incident</style>. A minor disaster, though I must admit, quite the spectacle! In the wake of it, dear <style="highlight">Zorya</style> and a few of our esteemed faculty members have proposed some rather inventive changes to our school rules.

One professor even suggested, and I quote, "At this rate, the students will blow the whole school up with their herbal tea!" Now, while I'm sure that's a bit of an exaggeration, the sight of a tea-flooded lecture hall was certainly unforgettable.

I do agree, though, that a revision is necessary.

So, here's my proposal: let's add water to the list of forbidden foods in Article 6, Clause 8. This, in theory, would make the brewing of herbal tea a tad more difficult, don't you think?

What say you, Professor Zorya? Does this solve our dilemma?

<style="highlight">... Such an unreasonable revision would lead to major disorder, Headmaster. It mustn't be passed.</style>

But this is the best solution I can think of, dear Zorya! If it's vetoed, we'll have no choice but to <u><link=Case><style="highlight">put the revision on hold</style></link></u>.

<style="highlight">... Let's put it off then.</style>

368.title: Eyes on You (1)
368.content:
I stumbled on that special mirror on a typical afternoon. It looked plain and worn, yet I felt an inexplicable pull toward it...
It was as if an enormous space lay beyond the surface, ready to swallow me if I looked too long...
It has to be a magic mirror.
...
Legend says that anyone who prays to the mirror will receive enlightenment.
Countless mages spend their entire lives searching for a magic mirror, and now one stands right before me. Yet I can't bring myself to decide… A voice in my head tells me that once I pray to it, something will change—irreversibly.
...
I prayed to the mirror.
...
I can feel my magic growing stronger... I've been enlightened! I'm about to go beyond my limits and reach a level I could never attain before!
...
<style="highlight">Someone's watching me.</style>

Someone's watching me. I'm sure of it. I can feel their eyes on me wherever I go.
I've exhausted every tracking method to my knowledge, but I still can't find the stalker...
...
Stop watching me! Stop it! Stop!
...
Who are you?
...
I've found it. It's everywhere—hidden in still water, on the surface of glass, in anything that reflects.
And it's staring at me through all the mirrors.
Ready to break free at any moment.
...
There it is. An exact replica of me emerges from the mirror.
It's the <style="highlight">mirror monster</style> that empowered my magic.
It takes hold of my hand and <style="highlight">shoves me into the mirror</style>.
Now... it has become "me".

369.title: Merlin's Memo
369.content:
... Cranky's working on a new treat for my afternoon tea. I hear it's a pie filled with fruit and cheese.

I consider cooking a kind of magic, but as skilled a mage as I am, I'm hopeless in the kitchen. Whoever invented it must have been an alchemical genius.

Cooking involves mixing the ingredients at the right proportions and adding suitable bases like water, oil, or wine. With seasoning herbs as catalysts, the mixture reacts under the heat of the fire elemental. This is alchemy even the common folk can enjoy!

A mouthwatering aroma is in the air, and I can't wait for afternoon tea! I hope Cranky remembers to drizzle extra honey on the pie.

While waiting, I should focus on work and ignore my rumbling tummy.

371.title: My Student Life
371.content:
... The new semester started, and of course, an awkward guy moved in next door. His name's Cyran, and for some reason, I swear he's got it out for me. I have no idea why.

He's super smart—probably the only one in our year who's almost as good as me. The gravity spell he refined? It can literally warp space to slow down enemies. Pretty impressive

After half a year, he's finally stopped glaring at me like I'm a monster. Sometimes he even talks to me now, usually about schoolwork. This morning, he walked past my desk four times and... did not say a single word. Eventually, I had to tap his shoulder and tell him, "Hey, you could've just said hi." His face went red so fast I thought he'd catch fire. Dura above, I didn't mean to scare him!

Anyway, after trying all my social "hacks"—small talk, compliments, bluffing, even a little teasing—he finally blurted out that he sees me as his rival and plans to beat me in the next exam.

I think he was serious, but seriously... can't a guy be more creative with his life goals? I told him there are way cooler things to try, like inventing the eleventh way to skip class. He just stared at me like I was speaking some ancient language. I'm pretty sure he didn't get it. So yeah... he's probably gonna take second place in finals again this year. By now he should've snapped out of it and gone back to his usual geeky self. Haha... classic Cyran.

If I pop by his door with some new magic tricks, he'll probably scowl and demand I teach him everything. And honestly? I kinda like that. What a wholesome, weird little friendship we've got.

I should get back to work!

373.title: Corruption Study
373.content:
... Human-to-Hypofiend transformations, commonly referred to as corruption, were recorded as early as the First Divine War. The Arcane Council has maintained ongoing studies of <style="highlight">corruption</style> since its establishment.

So far, we have identified the bodily changes that occur during corruption and have been able to slow them by suppressing mana absorption. These insights have paved the way for further advances in the sealing and purification of Hypofiends.

Based on these findings, I have refined my magic circle. Experiments show it is highly effective at <style="highlight">sealing</style> both common Hypofiends and even Hypogeans.

375.title: Select
375.content:
Once again, a sense of trepidation grips me. I feel as if I'm standing on the edge of a cliff, with a bottomless abyss looming before me.

I know that only mages with strong mental strength can sense danger.

Maybe this is my destiny. The war with the <style="highlight">Hypogeans</style> is certain to come.

Fear stirs within me. I'm afraid of conflict, death, and bloodshed. What if I could stop it before it happens?

... Turns out I'm actually not as prepared to <style="highlight">sacrifice myself</style> as I thought. Alright, "sacrifice" might sound too dramatic, but I have no idea how this war will end. Death might not even be the worst possible outcome.

I'll make my decision eventually, even though there's hardly any choice at all. I just hope my friends won't be too upset.

Maybe this is the responsibility that comes with the title of <style="highlight">Merlin</style>.

376.title: Deciphering Notes
376.content:
... I came into possession of a stele that predates the First Divine War. I am attempting to decipher its inscriptions, but without sufficient reference materials, progress has been slow.

"Life drifts through the sea of stars... (indecipherable) The Primordial Dragon arrives (indecipherable)"

The hieroglyphs for "light" and "star" bear a striking resemblance to the early symbols of Dura found within the Temple...

Next to them is a "scepter," which is often associated with royalty or authority... Could this inscription... be referring to Dura's divine power?

What truly unsettles me is this large symbol at the center, part of which appears to have been intentionally damaged. I can barely make out a few syllables.

"Ig...ti..." It could be a location or a name. Unfortunately, I can't be certain without finding more comparable inscriptions for analysis.

380.title: Gourmet Mage
380.content:
... Merlin has a sweet tooth, believing that sweets bring joy and that a cheerful mood is essential for mastering magic.

A cup of coffee must have three spoonfuls of sugar, and cupcakes are at their best when drizzled with tangy gooseberry sauce. On top of that, cookies should be served with a dollop of chocolate sauce.

Too much sugar might cause cavities or other health problems, you say? Well, Merlin believes all of that can be remedied with healing magic.

Of course, if you aren't a mage, you shouldn't attempt these recipes.

382.title: Merlin & the Lost Kingdom
382.content:
... Tears glistened in Alnina's eyes, her lips trembling as she struggled to hold them back. She was reluctant for the legendary mage to witness the sorrow of a princess on the verge of losing everything.
"Please," she clutched Merlin's arm, pleading. "My parents are gone... I cannot bear to see the kingdom they loved fall to ruin and sink beneath the sea..."
Merlin stared at Alnina without a word. The mage's eyes were brimming with deep pain and compassion.
"I'm only a mage, not a god," Merlin replied, looking into her eyes. "What has happened cannot be undone."
"Your kingdom... has been claimed by the sea."

394.title: Ancestral Sense
394.content:
This is an advanced <style="highlight">transfiguration technique for the wolf form</style>. If you transform into a hamster, rabbit, or bird, your ancestors will ignore you.

Ancestral Sense enables you to detect spirits or previously existing objects <style="highlight">within a certain range</style> and <style="highlight">interact</style> with them. Keep in mind that perception is mutual. The moment you see an entity, you become visible to it as well.

Practice daily until it becomes second nature. (Few can achieve this, but if you never try, you will never know.)

Lastly, you must have mental strength at the "Average" level (commonly known as "Level 3") in the Standard Mage's Mental Strength Assessment. Without it, your ancestors will ignore you!

Note: Avoid using Ancestral Sense in graveyards. You will regret it.

399.title: Important Statement
399.content:
Rumors of a so-called "kin of the fallen goddess" lurking in our lands are entirely unfounded. As the foremost authority on this matter, I issue this statement to set the record straight.

The <style="highlight">Gilded Serpent</style> was a humble offering I once presented at a living sacrifice to the Herdmaster. Displeased by its plain form, the deity bestowed upon it golden scales and three heads.

Despite its fearsome appearance, the Gilded Serpent is harmless. Should you encounter one of these rare creatures in the <style="highlight">swamps</style> at <style="highlight">midnight</style>, DO NOT harm it! The Herdmaster has fallen. Turning your anger upon innocent creatures serves neither justice nor reason.

414.title: Dear Oxana
414.content:
You always say I'll last forever. The truth is, before I met you, "forever" felt like a punishment. Day after day, I watched the world change and fade while I stayed the same—rotten and forgotten. Then you showed up and left flowers at my grave. You didn't flinch at my hideous face. You didn't shy away from my cold touch. And just like that, the heart in my chest—dead for a very long time—began to beat again.

I know you fear the mirror. You fear the day you see new lines and realize time is winning. But that's not what I see when I look at you. I see the girl in the snow who held out that wreath to me. I can't stop time. I can't keep it from taking what it takes. But I can do one thing well. I can stay by your side and protect every moment you're given. I'll do my best to make you less afraid of growing older, less afraid of goodbye. I want you to wake up every morning and feel happy you did.

I'll be with you until the day we have to part. That's my promise. It's the one kind of "forever" I can give you as a Graveborn.

<align="right">Always yours,
<align="right">Kiran

415.title: To Kiran
415.content:
To my forever love,

Before I started writing, I noticed the first fine line at the corner of my eye. I thought it would scare me, but it didn't. If anything, it felt like proof I've been smiling a lot since I met you.

You always say you're cold, but to me, you've never been that. You're the warmest person I've ever known. Being with you taught me what really matters in life: it's not living forever—it's the moments we share and remember.

So my most selfish wish isn't to live longer. It's that my time with you can make your forever feel a little warmer. I'm not asking for a promise that we'll never part. I just want us to savor every sunrise and every sunset we're given, and leave you with enough memories to make you smile the moment they return to you.

Promise me something. If I'm gone, don't shut the world out. Keep finding the good in it, like I'm still right there beside you. Take what we had and go see the world. Walk through those flower fields for me. Look forward to the spring that comes after the snow melts.

As long as the world still looks beautiful through your eyes, my love is still with you.

<align="right">With love,
<align="right">Oxana

416.content:

That day, deep in the forest, you saved a fragile life. To you, it was a simple act. To her, it was the moment the world lit up again.

My name is Sersha. It was your kindness that gave me the courage to write this letter.

My little sister Liselle is being held in a hidden place to the west. The entrance only appears <style="highlight">at night</style>, and only if you use <style="highlight">a special transfiguration spell</style>.

Maybe I shouldn't ask this of you... but I believe someone who once reached out to save a helpless life would do it again.

—Sersha, who has nowhere else to turn

435.title: On Sarethiel: 1
435.content:
Sarethiel used to be compassionate, bestowing his blessings upon his worshippers, asking nothing in return. Under his care, humanity thrived and prospered.
Now, the world lies in devastation, with humanity plagued by famine, floods, and swarms of locusts. Sarethiel names it punishment for their sins.
<style="highlight">The corruption has twisted Sarethiel</style> into a selfish and cruel god who demands tribute from those who worship him.
Although Tuttleton is in shambles, it was once home to his most devoted worshippers. Hence, it serves as the perfect place for him to hide and recuperate.
Yet several settlements surrounding Halia continue their devotion to the God of Harvest. He may seek them out to feed upon their faith...
435.content_male:

438.title: Plant Purifier
438.content:
Expected Effect:
Cleanses plants affected by harsh environments. When enchanted, it forms a lasting magic barrier that allows the plant to grow even without light or water.
Preparation:
Cut the tender stems of <style="highlight">emerald tendrils</style> into finger-joint lengths and gently crush them in a ceramic jar to extract their juice.
Slowly pour in the <style="highlight">salt lake brine</style>, stirring constantly until the liquid becomes an even pale green.
Finally, sprinkle in some sifted fine powder of <style="highlight">weathered granite soil</style>. Stir briefly, then let the mixture settle. Use only the clear liquid from the top.

472.title: Here Lies Torsen
472.content:
Here lies Torsen, a forcefield magic researcher and an unknown mage.
Torsen devoted himself to studying unconventional fields and endured the contempt of his peers. Now he rests here in solitude.
Fame may elude him, but his unwavering dedication to the pursuit of knowledge commands our respect.
Torsen was a student of the Serene Lyceum. The dust on his name must be lifted, and his diligence deserves recognition.
His remains have been laid to rest in the Lyceum Graveyard, where he shall know eternal peace.
May he be forever remembered by the professors and students of the Serene Lyceum.

476.title: For Hildi
476.content:
Dear Hildi,
My name is Pirand, and I've had a crush on you for quite some time.
I've been at the Lyceum for four years, but every time I see you, my spells just go haywire. Yesterday, I tried to conjure a rose for you and ended up with a talking cabbage instead. Rather than letting it do the talking, I think I should speak for myself.
Would you like to take a walk around the training grounds sometime? Or maybe hang out in the library? I could lend you my father's potion-making books with all his notes.
If you'd like to go on a little outing with me, turn your crucible anticlockwise three times during alchemy class. If not, turn it clockwise three times. Either way, no pressure—I'll respect your choice.

477.title: For Hildi
477.content:
The Starfall Lake draws its edges close in winter.
By the shore, I watch the fish swim in silence,
And joyful couples passing by, their youth a fleeting glimmer on the water's surface.
Meanwhile, I can only wonder which side of the sea holds you.
When I part the reeds that cloak my heart, I see you waiting there.
Everything falls into place, as if a long-forgotten, ancient spell has been cast.
The boundless sea within me recedes,
Shrinking into a lake to make room for your sky.

479.title: A Day in Our Routine
479.content:
Today, we once again helped a traveler lost in the forest.
As Talking Root retracted its spiky vines and lit the path with its glowing branches, I showed up at its cues to explain the forest's nature, calm the traveler, and guide them out.
That wasn't our first collaboration. After each successful rescue, I could sense Talking Root's relief, a serenity that made the forest breathe as one.
These days, Talking Root is brimming with vitality. It delights in watching the forest's creatures and dripping morning dew onto the birds' heads.
I hope it stays full of life forever and never knows loneliness in the years ahead.
Protecting this forest and seeing life thrive in magic alongside Talking Root is the life I've always dreamed of.

480.title: Perri's Last Letter
480.content:
Dear Talking Root,
By the time you read this letter, I may have already merged with the forest, maybe as a new patch of moss or a growing vine. It's natural to feel a little sad, but don't let grief overwhelm you.

I'm not gone forever, only existing in another form. Whenever the breeze brushes your face, the dew settles nearby, or the roots tremble, it is my whisper reaching you.

By the way, once you're feeling better, don't forget to visit the Serene Lyceum for treatment. The mages there will help you.

When you're well again, you will meet new friends who, like me, are eager to understand you.

Use your branches to ease their fear and your roots to steady the trembling ground, just as we once did.

485.content:
Dear Master <style="stress"><player_name></style>,
It's been 50 days since you left. Our tribe is slowly recovering from the aftermath of the fallen goddess and the war, thanks to Merlin and Morgan's help. I've made some progress with my magic, but there's still a long way to go before I can catch up to you, of course...
After Azora's fall, Kordan suggested throwing away the bed prepared for the goddess, but I insisted on keeping it. It was where you rested... I won't let anyone change a thing in that room, not even a single flower.
Also, I made two dolls of us. Whenever I see them together, it feels like you're right here beside me...
I can't wait for the day we see each other again.
…………………………
Dear Master <style="stress"><player_name></style>,
It's been 73 days since you left.
I'm getting better at magic. Merlin and Morgan say that if I stay committed, I'll soon be able to handle things on my own. Even so, I feel you're still far ahead of me.
When will I be able to start learning temporal magic? Maybe then I'll have a chance to see you again. I could use the power left behind by the fallen goddess...
You haven't been gone for long, but I already miss you so much...
I hope you're doing well in the future.
…………………………
Dear Master <style="stress"><player_name></style>,
I'll be leaving the tribe soon.
According to Merlin, the other gods around the world are showing signs of corruption. To prevent them from endangering mortals, they must be dealt with quickly. As the God of Harvest is still at large, Merlin has decided that Morgan will hold down the fort while she and I set out to take down the gods.
Be assured that I'll give my all to protect my tribe and the world you saved.
Before I leave, please allow me to take your doll with me. With it by my side, it feels as though you're supporting me from the future.
As for the "Gala doll", I'll leave it on your bed in the Great Treehouse, so when you return, you'll see me waiting for you...

This mild potion can quickly repair minor damage to magical creations and restore the flow of their mana.

488.title: Old Notebook
488.content:
I can't stop thinking about what happened today.

My most outstanding student collapsed in the study room, still clutching an unfinished magical circle draft. He had gone without rest for days to complete his research.

I can hear whispers coming from the corridor. They say I pushed him too hard, and my coursework was too demanding.

The school hasn't accused me of anything, but I can sense their doubts. Still, it is my own conscience that weighs heaviest on me.

I was so focused on helping my students master higher-level magic that I failed to consider their limits.

Last night, a nightmare haunted my sleep. In it, my body grew cold and rigid, and papers sprouted from my back like wings. I had become a book Hypofiend.

I waved papers and ink, urging my students to run faster down the hallway.

Their pace became frantic, their breathing ragged, but I couldn't bring myself to stop.

<align="right">Professor Movan

I've always believed that demanding constant diligence from my students was the surest way to secure their future.

But reality hits hard. Time and again, I've had to witness the weight proving too much for them to bear.

The collapsed student is a wake-up call. It seems the path of growth can also be a slope leading straight into an abyss.

I dread the day when their eyes reflect nothing but exhaustion.

My health is failing, and a relentless cough won't leave me. I want to stop, but it's already too late.

If there were a next life, I'd be a teacher who listens, rather than a shepherd who drives the flock with a whip.

I was so focused on helping my students master higher-level magic that I failed to consider their limits.

Last night, a nightmare haunted my sleep. In it, my body grew cold and rigid, and papers sprouted from my back like wings. I had become a book Hypofiend.

I waved papers and ink, urging my students to run faster down the hallway.

Their pace became frantic, their breathing ragged, but I couldn't bring myself to stop.

<align="right">Professor Movan

I've always believed that demanding constant diligence from my students was the surest way to secure their future.

But reality hits hard. Time and again, I've had to witness the weight proving too much for them to bear.

The collapsed student is a wake-up call. It seems the path of growth can also be a slope leading straight into an abyss.

I dread the day when their eyes reflect nothing but exhaustion.

My health is failing, and a relentless cough won't leave me. I want to stop, but it's already too late.

If there were a next life, I'd be a teacher who listens, rather than a shepherd who drives the flock with a whip.

<align="right">Cedrik Orwin

489.title: About Talking Root
489.content:
I named this towering tree <style="highlight">"Talking Root"</style>, in honor of the deepest connection between life and the land. This name is known only between the tree and me. <style="highlight">Anyone who can speak its name is deemed a trustworthy friend.</style> As the oldest tree in the forest, its roots have thrived in this magic-rich soil for centuries, allowing it to grow into a sentient, intelligent being.
Before I found it, it had been lonely and despondent, having no one in the forest to talk to.
I visit it regularly, sharing stories from the outside world and singing songs to revere the forest. It responds with the sway of its branches and the shifting patterns of its bark, expressing its emotions in its own language.
We have forged a special friendship, built on trust and companionship.

499.title: Valen's Letter
499.content:
Dear Magister Merlin,

How are you holding up in Savannah? From what I hear, the place's been in utter chaos lately, with a temple vanishing, a missing princess, and that whole sword‑in‑the‑stone affair. Meanwhile, I'm sipping fine wine and catching wind of your exploits from hundreds of miles away. I must say, your stories are far juicier than any minstrel's tale!

Knowing you, I can already picture you working yourself to the bone to set things straight.
You're busy combing through every nook and cranny for hidden information, aren't you?

I know you'll likely brush this off, but still, I must warn you to keep your distance from the Solitaries.
Sure, they're just a harmless civilian organization, but dealing with them... is a real pain.
They don't care about gold or do things for favors; they only have their eyes on other people's secrets.
Be prepared to be stripped bare if you want anything from them. Honestly, I'd rather beat the answers out of them than sit through their questioning.

... But then again, you'd probably say it's worth going through all that if it means finding the truth.
Fine, if you insist on visiting them, I can point you to the right path—though whether it's the path you should take is another matter.

Make your way to <style="highlight">Vina Cemetery</style>, just outside the city.
<style="highlight">Seek out a unique coffin, open it, and lie down inside</style>.
Don't worry, it's just their special way of welcoming their guests. It's a bit cramped and stuffy inside, but just think of it as an early taste of your afterlife. After all, there are few quiet spots like this in Savannah.

Good luck, Magister. Hopefully, you'll still have a few secrets left when you climb out of that coffin.

Yours sincerely, Valen

500.title: Meeting Minutes
500.content:
Scribe: Adrian Crawley

Subject: Fortress Council Site Selection and Construction

Five days ago, our provisional command center came under another surprise attack. Thanks to timely reinforcements led by <style="highlight">Rion and Ryan</style>, we successfully repelled the assault. However, the Hypogeans' infiltration tactics have become increasingly sophisticated. With our command center now compromised, any further attack could prove catastrophic.

To address this issue, <style="highlight">Commander Rolan</style> proposed using our current command center as bait to ensnare the enemy. Meanwhile, a fully concealed and heavily fortified alternate command center will be built at a separate location.

Following extensive site surveys, the new command center will be established within a residential building in Savannah. The structure, abandoned during the war, offers an inconspicuous exterior while providing ample interior space. Minimal renovations are required to make it operationally functional.

In accordance with Commander Rolan's directives, the perimeter of the command center shall be covertly secured, and a specialized access mechanism will be installed at the entrance to restrict entry to senior officers only. All personnel involved in the refurbishment are prohibited from disclosing any details of the site.

Commander Rolan has designated the new command center the Fortress Council, a name chosen to reflect its role as an unassailable stronghold protecting our military interests.

May Dura's divine light restore peace to our homeland...

501.title: Battle Report
501.content:
Scribe: Oliver Emery

... When the Mirror Wraith appeared, darkness engulfed the battlefield as though all light had been consumed by its shadow. As countless Hypofiends surged forth, our morale collapsed to its lowest point.

Commander Rolan raised the sword granted by Dura and advanced alone to the front. "For our homeland!" His cry echoed across the plain.

Then came the miracle. Like the rising sun, Commander Rolan radiated a golden light that dispelled the fear gripping our soldiers' hearts.

The battle commenced. <style="highlight">General Reinhold, alongside vanguard commanders Rion and Ryan</style>, charged into the ranks of the Hypofiends like three bolts of lightning. They tore through the horde, opening a path for our main force to advance.

Commander Rolan engaged the Mirror Wraith in fierce combat, each swing of his blade imbued with sacred force. When the Mirror Wraith finally collapsed, the entire plain sank into deathly silence, shattered moments later by thunderous cheers from our soldiers.

Victory is ours this time, but the war is far from over.

Beneath the setting sun, Commander Rolan stood among the fallen, leaning upon his sword for support. His silhouette would echo through the ages as an undying legend.

<style="highlight">Seek out a unique coffin, open it, and lie down inside</style>.
Don't worry, it's just their special way of welcoming their guests. It's a bit cramped and stuffy inside, but just think of it as an early taste of your afterlife. After all, there are few quiet spots like this in Savannah.

Good luck, Magister. Hopefully, you'll still have a few secrets left when you climb out of that coffin.

Yours sincerely,
Valen

503.title: Silken Snare Menu
503.content:
<style="highlight">◆SOUPS◆</style>
Nightmist Bisque
Midnight mushrooms and shadow truffles from Whiteridge, finely ground and gently simmered in a delicate stock. Each spoonful embodies the forest's vitality.

Amber Consomme
Clarified over 48 hours, stripping away all impurities to preserve only the ingredient's essence. Gleams like molten gold.

<style="highlight">◆APPETIZERS◆</style>

Light as air, it melts on the tongue, leaving behind notes of vanilla.

Red wine laced with a touch of passionflower nectar. Perfect for nights of quiet romance.

Clear sparkling water adorned with edible luminescent petals. Sweet and invigorating.

507.content:
To our friend far away, Merlin,

Happy Emberlight Festival. I hope you're doing well, wherever you are. Carolina, Ludovic, and the rest of us have been thinking about you.

Ever since Shemira's family settled in Whiteridge, something about this silent land has started to change. It's still a place for the undead and the forgotten, but somehow, it feels a little less cold than before. People who used to keep to themselves now gather beneath the eaves of Ludovic's manor, speaking in hushed voices, trading long-forgotten memories. Maybe that's the true gift of the Emberlight Festival this year—the return of life.

Now that the festival is here, all of us—Ludovic, Carolina, Callan, Shemira, Niru, little Daimon, and plenty of others whose names you might not remember—have gathered together at Everstill Manor. The fire crackles in the hearth, its warm light brightening up faces that once looked so lonely. We may not be able to join the living in their celebrations, nor set foot in Avalon, but in spirit, we're already there celebrating with everyone, across the boundaries of life and death.

I hope this letter reaches you, carried by the warmth of Emberlight. And may its light guide you through every step of the year ahead.

Your eternal friend,
Valka
Eve of the Emberlight Festival, at Everstill Manor

508.title: Upper Circle Insider
508.content:
A neon carp worth a staggering one million gold has made a splash in the fish market, stirring widespread interest among the nobles!

Baron Grandet, its current owner, made a public statement at his residence in the upper district:

"... This is no ordinary fish! It's a <style="highlight">neon carp</style> valued at one million gold!" The affluent nobleman emphasized, "One million gold!"

According to the baron, the fish is a rare variant of carp. Its worth lies not in its appearance, but in its medicinal properties...

Neon carp soup is said to <style="highlight">cure all ailments and grant immortality</style>.

The ailing King Maximilian is the first thought that comes to mind when one speaks of this fish.

Due to His Majesty's critical condition, the Queen has assumed the regency. However, Her Majesty appears to lack the requisite political acumen.

To date, Her Majesty has resolved neither the succession dispute nor the escalating tensions along the borders with Bantus.

If the fish is indeed the right cure for His Majesty, Savannah's political landscape may be poised for another upheaval!

In the meantime, one cannot help but question whether the royal court has truly done enough to cure the king, when a baron can acquire the remedy with such ease.

Could the Queen be reluctant to relinquish power? Or is Her Majesty deliberately delaying the King's recovery to secure an advantage for Princess Peggy in the succession?

509.title: Grandet's Letter
509.content:
Your Majesty,

Since receiving word of His Majesty's grave condition, I have been consumed with such concern that I have found no rest at night.

Even the finest king salmon at breakfast could not distract me from thoughts of His Majesty's exemplary governance. Each time I closed my eyes to rest, I found myself recalling his countless contributions to Savannah's prosperity.

Even while watching the ballet performance by the famous Pavlova, my thoughts remained with His Majesty...

Ah, what would become of Savannah without His Majesty at the helm? And what a heavy burden would then fall upon Your Majesty! At this thought, I was brought to tears and overcome with emotion...

Thus, I dispatched my men far and wide in search of a cure for the King. At last, my efforts have borne fruit!

I have found an exceedingly rare fish known as the neon carp, whose broth is said to grant eternal youth and cure all ailments.

It cost me one million gold, but for the sake of His Majesty and Your Majesty, every gold was well spent!

However, given the fish's fragile nature, I was reluctant to risk transporting it myself. So, I have kept it in a river close to my residence.

I humbly request that Your Majesty dispatch a guard to <style="highlight">the river near the upper district's arched bridge</style> <style="highlight">tomorrow morning</style> to collect the fish.

Your faithful servant, Baron Grandet

520.title: The Savannah Eye
520.content:
—Issue No. 132—
<style="stress">[Hall of Ancients Latest Updates!]</style>
<style="stress">[Mysterious Court Mage Linked to the Queen]</style>
By: Blind Mole Rat

Following Princess Peggy's failed attempt to draw the sword in the Hall of Ancients, another key figure has stepped into the spotlight—Cassadee, the court mage who accompanied her!

Our investigation reveals that Cassadee is merely a novice mage. Following her predecessor's suspicious death, she was swiftly appointed with the backing of the Queen and Princess Peggy.

Is this just a coincidence? The testimony from an anonymous insider casts everything in doubt.

"I saw it with my own eyes!" the eyewitness said, their voice trembling with fear. "Cassadee pulled out a bizarre device in the chapel! After she chanted over it, that thing began to give off an ominous glow and sound... Then all hell broke loose!"

According to our sources within the court, the Queen has been steadily consolidating her influence among the court mages over the years. It is now said that more than half the cohort stands aligned with her.

Is Cassadee a key piece in the Queen's plans? Could the disappearance of the Hall of Ancients be part of a grander design by Her Majesty?

The Savannah Eye brings you every development in the royal capital as it happens!

—Issue No. 132—
<style="stress">[Exclusive! The Unspeakable Horrors Inside the Hall of Ancients!]</style>
By: Gray Raccoon

As the mystery surrounding the disappearance of the Hall of Ancients deepens, the royal court remains a wall of silence. An exclusive interview with an anonymous royal clerk who returned from the chapel unveils disturbing details never before disclosed...

"At that moment," he recalled, his voice strained with fear, "everyone was praying Princess Peggy would draw the sword and inherit the throne. But Her Highness… she just smiled."

"It was... a cold, knowing smile of triumph that sent chills down my spine. I had a feeling she didn't care whether she could draw the sword at all… because what she truly wanted was something else!"

The royal clerk later described an even more astonishing scene when King Rolan appeared to quell the crisis following Princess Peggy's failed attempt to draw the sword.

"When King Rolan appeared, the smile on the princess' face disappeared, replaced by a look of sheer panic, as though her plot had just been exposed. Rather than showing reverence for her ancestor, her eyes darted uneasily!"

The royal clerk's statement offers a new perspective on the incident. It raises questions about Princess Peggy's possible involvement in the disappearance of the Hall of Ancients, suggesting a conspiracy far-reaching enough to alter the empire's fate.

The Savannah Eye will keep you updated!

We welcome members of the public to provide leads or information to us.

Reach us at: <style="highlight">The mailbox by the tablet in Savannah's central plaza</style>

524.title: The Savannah Eye
524.content:
—Issue No. 136—
<style="stress">[Early Signs of the Hall of Ancients Conspiracy!]</style>
<style="stress">[Peggy Hides After Plot Exposed!]</style>
By: Brown Bear

Was the Hypofiend onslaught in the Hall of Ancients truly an accident? Through exclusive interviews with multiple eyewitnesses, we have uncovered a shocking allegation: Princess Peggy's attempt to draw Excalibur was not an act of desperation, but a long-planned bid for the throne!

"The situation wasn't nearly that critical," a noble present at the scene stated. "The Hypofiends caused some disruption, but not enough to warrant the use of Excalibur." This indicates that while things were still under control, Princess Peggy's first thought was to reach for the sword that signifies royal authority.

Was that really a spur-of-the-moment act? For more information, we managed to locate a court tutor who once instructed the princess. She confirmed, "The princess had little interest in the history of the royal family, but recently, she's shown an unusual enthusiasm for the Excalibur ceremony and inquiring about its details with multiple people."

Now, the truth is beginning to emerge. The Hypofiend attack was highly likely just a pretext to legitimize the princess' contact with the sacred sword, allowing her to bypass the prince in the line of succession and seize the throne.

The divine manifestation of King Rolan may be interpreted as a warning against the alleged scheme. As for Princess Peggy's disappearance, it may not have been accidental, but rather a deliberate choice to vanish and evade public condemnation.

A meticulously orchestrated power play was derailed by an ancestor's wrath. What course of action will the Queen and her daughter take next?

Peer into the royal family's power play with The Savannah Eye!

525.title: The Chapel Is Back!
525.content:
[Prince Orion: The Chosen One!]

JUST IN! A divine phenomenon happened in Savannah today, leaving the entire city stunned!

At noon, a magical shield enclosed the central plaza, and the long-lost Hall of Ancients reappeared within it, fully intact where it once stood.

And the hero who brought it back is none other than Prince Orion! Driven by concern for his missing sister and the honor of the royal family, he defeated the formidable Mirror Wraith and overcame Dura's trials to be named her chosen!

As Excalibur appeared upon the central plaza's platform, Prince Orion emerged from the Hall of Ancients and took hold of its hilt. In the next instant, the blade acknowledged his will and slid free from the stone.

Golden rays burst forth and shot skyward, scattering the dark clouds above! The entire plaza was bathed in a warm, divine radiance—a sacred moment witnessed by all of Savannah.

Without a doubt, Dura and the kings of old have made their choice!

The Lightbearer Empire will rise again in glory under a rightful ruler!

Together, let us witness the dawn of this great era!

(Note: To be published as a front-page story upon the Hall of Ancients' return.)

526.title: Weekly Pitch List
526.content:
Story 1: The Untold Truth Behind the Late Queen's Death
Evaluation: Rejected. Too risky as it involves the prince and could backfire.

Story 2: Who Tried to Kill Prince Orion During the Hunt?
Evaluation: Approved. Make the headline more eye-catching and emphasize the prince's bravery and composure under pressure. Avoid detailing how the Hypofiend was defeated, and do not mention Gwyneth.

Story 3: Why Has the King Not Recovered? Royal Physician Linked to the Queen!
Evaluation: Approved. Proceed with caution due to the high level of public attention. Fabricate anonymous sources to imply that the king's illness may not be as straightforward as it appears.

Story 4: The Mischievous Princess and Her Noble Victims!
Evaluation: Approved. Keep it as backup content. Replace "mischievous" with a more contentious term upon publication.

Conclusion: Viscount Demit was dissatisfied with both the quality and quantity of the story pitches, warning that performance bonuses could be canceled. Each reporter is required to submit ten new topic proposals at the next meeting. Anyone unable to do so "need not bother coming to work anymore" (quoted verbatim).

530.title: Help Prince Orion
530.content:
This is Merlin. Prince Orion has left Savannah for the time being, but his presence lingers in our hearts. As his trusted friend, I am secretly preparing for his return to power.

And I need sufficient resources to execute my grand plan!

Now, I am short of just 500 more gold to inscribe a magic circle powerful enough to bring the prince back in power.

If all goes well, the prince will return by ship to reclaim his throne. He will need your help—not merely as a supporter, but as one of his most trusted allies.

Each gold you contribute counts! Let us work together for His Highness' glorious return!

If you are willing to contribute, bring 500 gold to the docks in the commoners' district. Seek out a cargo ship bearing a staff emblem on its sail and hand the funds to my assistant. Prince Orion will arrive at the docks at dusk tomorrow to meet you.

Your friend,
Merlin

"Prince Orion's future lies in your hands!"

535.title: Morning Post Headline
535.content:
<style="stress">[Viscount Demit Confesses All!]</style>
By: Maska

Viscount Demit, the mastermind behind The Savannah Eye, has confessed to all his crimes!

This fallen nobleman secretly founded the seditious newspaper with massive financial support from a mysterious benefactor. He put together a team of ex-convicts to fabricate and spread vicious rumors targeting the Queen and Princess Peggy.

As his plot crumbled, Viscount Demit exploited his municipal authority and attempted to flee by water. He was subsequently apprehended by relevant authorities.

While Viscount Demit now faces prosecution, credible evidence suggests darker, more powerful forces remain at large. Stay tuned with us for further updates!

<style="stress">[Savannah Intrigue]</style>
<style="stress">[The Intern Reporter]</style>
Author: Haria

Character Introduction
Philippa: An energetic and inquisitive intern reporter. Though sometimes scatterbrained, she possesses keen intuition and a dauntless spirit. While investigating a missing girl case, she stumbles into a world of magic and danger.
Nightshade: A mysterious and formidable mage with a troubled past and a gentle nature. Moved by Philippa's innocence and determination, he chooses to join her investigation. Unaware of it himself, he has a soft spot for Philippa.
Alois: A castle-dwelling vampire noble and the prime suspect in the missing girl case. Said to be strikingly handsome and elegant yet cold and ruthless, he guards secrets that must never be revealed.
...
Philippa quickly pieced it together. "The castle is located on an isolated island, with no bridge connecting it to the mainland... So, those missing girls could only have reached it by water!"

As he listened to her well-reasoned analysis, a hint of admiration appeared in Nightshade's eyes.

Following this lead, it didn't take them long to discover an unregistered ship that departed from the old docks every midnight.

With a gentle flick of his fingers, Nightshade turned himself and Philippa into two fluffy little hamsters. They slipped onto that mysterious ship without anyone noticing.

The two hamsters huddled together in a dark corner, keeping each other warm. Amused, Nightshade commented, "Being a hamster suits you well."

Nightshade's voice briefly pulled Philippa back to the present, but her thoughts had already drifted to the moonlit castle on the island. The castle's master, Count Alois... was he truly as cold and merciless as the rumors claimed? Or was there more beneath his icy exterior?
...
(Don't miss the next supplement issue for the next chapter!)

541.title: Purification Potion
541.content:
This potion is made using three corrupted fungi: <style="highlight">mooncaps, rotcaps, and dustbane</style>. First, dry the <style="highlight">mooncaps</style> and grind them into a fine powder. Then roast the <style="highlight">rotcaps</style> over a low flame to draw out their essence. Finally, mix everything with the liquid extracted from <style="highlight">dustbane</style> and let the blend crystallize on its own.

It's a highly specialized remedy, designed to neutralize corrupted matter and reverse mutation. If the forest is ever to return to what it once was, this potion is the key.

542.title: About Talking Root
542.content:
I named this towering tree <style="highlight">"Talking Root"</style>, in honor of the deepest connection between life and the land. This name is known only between the tree and me. <style="highlight">Anyone who can speak its name is deemed a trustworthy friend.</style> As the oldest tree in the forest, its roots have thrived in this magic-rich soil for centuries, allowing it to grow into a sentient, intelligent being.
Before I found it, it had been lonely and despondent, having no one in the forest to talk to.
I visit it regularly, sharing stories from the outside world and singing songs to revere the forest. It responds with the sway of its branches and the shifting patterns of its bark, expressing its emotions in its own language.
We have forged a special friendship, built on trust and companionship.

543.title: A Day in Our Routine
543.content:
Today, we once again helped a traveler lost in the forest.
As Talking Root retracted its spiky vines and lit the path with its glowing branches, I showed up at its cues to explain the forest's nature, calm the traveler, and guide them out.
That wasn't our first collaboration. After each successful rescue, I could sense Talking Root's relief, a serenity that made the forest breathe as one.
These days, Talking Root is brimming with vitality. It delights in watching the forest's creatures and dripping morning dew onto the birds' heads.
I hope it stays full of life forever and never knows loneliness in the years ahead.
Protecting this forest and seeing life thrive in magic alongside Talking Root is the life I've always dreamed of.

544.title: Forest Crisis Alert
544.content:
Recently, <style="highlight">a mysterious dark force has been corrupting the forest</style>, seeping into Talking Root's mind like a toxin.
Talking Root has grown disoriented and even occasionally <style="highlight">attacked nearby creatures indiscriminately</style>. Clearly, this loss of control is the result of the dark force.
Under my care, Talking Root has shown signs of recovery, but the corruption has taken a heavy toll on its strength.
Now, it spends most of its time in deep sleep, and its waking hours continue to grow shorter.
I have decided to stay in the forest and care for it until it fully recovers.

545.title: Perri's Last Letter
545.content:
Dear Talking Root,
By the time you read this letter, I may have already merged with the forest, maybe as a new patch of moss or a growing vine. It's natural to feel a little sad, but don't let grief overwhelm you.

I'm not gone forever, only existing in another form. Whenever the breeze brushes your face, the dew settles nearby, or the roots tremble, it is my whisper reaching you.

By the way, once you're feeling better, don't forget to visit the Serene Lyceum for treatment. The mages there will help you.

When you're well again, you will meet new friends who, like me, are eager to understand you.

Use your branches to ease their fear and your roots to steady the trembling ground, just as we once did.

When you're well again, you will meet new friends who, like me, are eager to understand you.

Use your branches to ease their fear and your roots to steady the trembling ground, just as we once did.  

<align="right">Your eternal friend, Perri

547.title: Beat the Flood
547.content:
The flood brings devastation to our homeland.
Yet from the fertile soil it leaves behind, we grow our food.
Food gives us the strength to rebuild our homes.
Each time the flood strikes, we just bounce back stronger.
This is how we endure!
We have never conquered the flood; we have simply learned to live with it.

552.title: Untold History
552.content:
(Transcribed from an unknown source)
... Not all who ascend the throne are born with the talent to rule. Even the purest heir had to hone their skills alone at night. I myself witnessed a young ruler, burdened with the immense weight of crown and name, pacing <style="highlight">beneath the chamber drapes</style>, seeking the guidance of the dawn...

... ⎕⎕⎕⎕ answered his silent prayer. <style="highlight">Where candlelight and shadow became one</style>, the path to the Land of Bones opened...

The trial ended as night fell. <style="highlight">The Feather of Truth, the Coin of Prosperity, the Harp of Solace, and the Crown of Thorns</style>... All four relics required for the <style="highlight">Wisdom Spell</style> were finally in place...

Bathed in morning light, the young heir had become a true king, bearing newfound insight and wisdom beyond his years. Yet such blessings never come without a price...

553.title: Anti-Fever Elixir
553.content:
Crush the <style="highlight">frostmist herb</style>, extract its juice, and pour it into the crucible.
Slowly add the <style="highlight">calming essence</style>, stirring clockwise until the mixture turns a pale silvery-blue.
Just before the mixture boils, sprinkle in the <style="highlight">pinecone powder</style>.
Remove the mixture from the heat immediately, then bottle once it has cooled.

555.title: Theater Playbill
555.content:
Theater Playbill (Ascension Festival Edition)
King Rolan
During the darkest hour of the First Divine War, Rolan rallies both commoners and nobles to launch a counterattack against the Hypogeans.
Witness how Rolan becomes the light that dispels darkness.

Memoirs of a Veteran
"When the Hypogeans attacked, those nobles did nothing but whine like pigs in a pen."
"The only right thing they did was put their trust in that young man named Rolan!"

Rolan: Into the Night
At a grand ball, Rolan, the star of the evening, glides through the crowd of nobles.
He politely declines invitations to dance from beautiful noblewomen and pays no heed to the singer's alluring voice.
After handing his wineglass to the guard at the entrance, he slips into the night, drawn by a secret waiting beyond...

558.content:

He dispelled the mist with his sword, bringing forth Dura's divine light.
He built an entire empire from the ground up.
Now, we live in a prosperous city, study in well-equipped schools, and speak our minds freely.
It is because we remember.
We inherit both his triumph and the hopeful future he envisioned.

567.title: Carrie's Letter
567.content:
Dear Fessia,
It surprises even me that I feel like writing to you. Maybe it's because I still consider myself part of the Serene Lyceum.
I've heard about the terrible illness spreading at school, and I'm worried about you.
To be honest, I regret the choice I made back then. It not only stripped me of my magic but also left me with a frail body and the judgment of others.
I'm deeply concerned that this speech loss condition might put you all at risk. If you can, could you give everyone a heads-up on my behalf?
For us mages, talent determines how fast we progress, but only hard work determines how far we can go.
There are no shortcuts when it comes to magic.
Now, I've lost my chance to continue pursuing magic, whether through jealousy or misplaced hope. Still, I sincerely hope you can walk that path and see it through.
<align="right">Carrie, with deep regret

<style="stress">Research ID:</style> S-E5003
<style="stress">Research Title:</style> Automated Document Indexing and Classification Through Mana Resonance
Objective: The Arcane Affairs Office has been operating inefficiently, mainly due to the excessive time spent handling routine paperwork. This spell aims to use a low-energy mana field to automatically identify keywords in files and categorize documents by priority.

<style="stress">Observations:</style>
1.5 units of arcane catalyst provide sufficient coverage for all filing cabinets in the office.
By presetting relevant keywords (e.g., mana, border, research), the spell automatically sorts matching documents into their designated zones.

581.title: Dark Magic Research Notes
581.content:
[Evolution of Dark Magic]
Phase 1: <style="highlight">Flesh Binding Curse (Initial Form)</style>
Flaw: Can only be used between direct blood relatives, and the caster faces an immense risk of backlash.
Evaluation: Primitive, inefficient, and overly restrictive.

Phase 2: <style="highlight">Dark Transfer (Advanced Form)</style>
Breakthrough: Can now be used beyond direct blood relatives.
Flaw: The recipient must still "willingly" accept the repercussions.

Phase 3: <style="highlight">Dark Extraction (Perfected Form)</style>
... the third phase of research is nearing completion. Unlike the previous two phases, the spell can now extract power without consent.
No magical pact or consent is required. Once certain conditions are met, the recipient can forcibly transfer the repercussions and curse to a third party while stripping them of their power.

First Experiment (Completed)
Subject: <style="highlight">X (Emerson)</style>
Result: <style="highlight">Successful</style>
Procedure: Despite X's fierce resistance, the extraction was still successful. His mana was forcibly removed, draining his life force in an instant. His death was disguised as magical backlash. No one suspected a thing.

Ultimate Test
Subject: <style="highlight">M</style>
M meets every criterion for an ideal subject, from exceptionally pure mana circuits to an extraordinarily resilient soul. The only obstacles are the subject's immense mana reserves and exceptional mental fortitude.

Solution:
Construct an ultra-advanced empowerment magic circle and lure M into its core. This will suppress the flow of M's mana, making the extraction much easier.

Progress: <style="highlight">80%. The core runes have yet to be completed.</style>
Status: Cannot be activated yet

582.title: Special Edition
582.content:
<style="stress">[Savannah Intrigue: The Intern Reporter]</style>
...
To Nightshade's dismay, his magic faltered within the castle. Meanwhile, Alois conjured crimson thorns from the ground, instantly weaving them into an inescapable cage that trapped Nightshade within.
"Just give up, mage." Without sparing a glance at Nightshade, Alois strode toward the ballroom. "The lady's my partner for the evening."
When Philippa finally awoke, she found herself slumped across a long table laid with exquisite silverware and untouched food. A grand feast seemed poised to commence.
From the other end of the table, Alois' deep, velvety voice drifted over. He sat with composed ease, his brooding gaze fixed upon her.
"Philippa, you look so much like a lost lamb... You see, I've prepared the feast especially for you. Shall we begin?"
Horrified, Philippa searched the cavernous hall for Nightshade, but glimpsed only the flicker of candlelight.
"Where's Nightshade? What did you do to him?!" At the thought of his barely healed injuries, Philippa, for the first time, regretted involving him in this.
"Finish this dance with me, and you'll get to see that annoying bug."
With a gentle tap of his pale fingertips in the air, a waltz suddenly echoed throughout the hall.
Philippa's body moved of its own accord, following Alois' lead, yet her eyes continued to search the hall.
As the music reached its climax, Alois was ready to bend down and kiss the back of Philippa's hand…
*Rumble*
A thunderous explosion rocked the hall, as the cage of thorns shattered into a rain of splinters. When the dust settled, Nightshade emerged, wreathed in blue magical flames.
His eyes, once tender, now burned with cold, lethal rage.
A sinister smile spread across Alois' face. "Ha... things are getting interesting."
...

585.title: Here Lies Walter
585.content:
A drunkard named Gould found him on the streets.
A temple devotee cleansed his body.
A distant relative arrived and spoke his name.
Walter was but a fleeting shadow in the mortal world.


Written by: Gould the Busybody
Gould was a fixture at the tavern, never leaving before closing time.
One night, on his way home, he stumbled over Walter's body in the street and called for the guards to carry it to the temple.
To clear himself of suspicion, Gould paid a silver coin for a temple devotee to cleanse the corpse.
A distant relative eventually arrived to identify the body, only to disappear the moment funeral expenses were mentioned.
Left with no other choice, Gould spent another five silver coins on the cheapest plot in Vina Cemetery.
To make sure his money was well-spent, Gould carved his name into Walter's epitaph.

601.title: Monkey Spell
601.content:
Transfiguration, a common form of magic and an essential discipline for all mages, has a wide range of practical applications.

Fundamentally, this spell enables the caster to alter a target's shape and appearance. Skilled practitioners can even achieve cross-species transformation.

This article will delve into animal transfiguration, which grants rapid movement and the ability to communicate with animals.

Current academic consensus holds that animal transfiguration carries a significant risk: casters may struggle to revert to human form if their mental state becomes unstable.

However, in my opinion, this "risk" can be an advantage in certain situations.

Now, think back to your days at school. When you were snowed under with homework, did you ever envy the birds soaring freely in the sky?

Even after graduating, balancing work and life can be exhausting. Haven't you ever wished you could sleep the day away like your pet cat?

How long have we been pushed to live up to the expectations imposed on us as humans? At times, we cannot help but wonder whether evolution was a boon or a bane.

For some of us, what we truly need is to regress into monkeys! I believe there should be a spell to help us achieve that!

Therefore, I am attempting to permanently transform myself into a monkey through transfiguration. Once I succeed, the first thing I will do is wreak havoc on my supervisor's desk...

With the hands of a monkey, of course!

For your information, deep within Darkmire Cliff in <style="highlight">eastern Novaris</style> lies the <style="highlight">Refinery</style>. Within it rests the <style="highlight">Soul Forge</style>, a device jointly built by the Adamant Syndicate and the Bantus to transform the living into Graveborn bound to their service.

Please destroy it without delay to keep the living from harm.

607.content:
Dear Merlin,

I learned about your recent visit to the Gravebloom Fields and your encounter with a candle blossom-infected human. I have some important information regarding this matter.

The <style="highlight">Adamant Syndicate</style> plotted to spread the candle blossom plague throughout the Lightbearer Empire by distributing the flowers at the Seasong Theater. The harmful effects of candle blossom on the living are as follows:

(Below is a small piece of trimmed paper, written in handwriting completely different from the text above.)



Upon contact with a living being, candle blossoms immediately begin parasitic growth, draining the host's vitality. Symptoms may include hallucinations, numbness, or total loss of the senses. Once the flowers spread throughout the entire body, the host will die.

After the host dies, <style="highlight">the flowers will spread outward from the place of death</style> in search of new hosts. As such, an <style="highlight">outbreak</style> is inevitable if they are brought into areas densely populated by the living.

These properties allow the Graveborn to use candle blossoms to dispose of severed limbs that still retain traces of vitality. The flowers have little effect on the Graveborn, presumably because they repel the force of death that sustains the Graveborn.



(The handwriting below reverts to that of the previous paragraphs.)

The shapeshifting spell used to disguise the human stowaways is derived from the force of death, so they won't be infected until the spell wears off. Since they will remain in Novaris until the show ends, there is no cause for concern for the time being. Keep up your disguise and stay safe.

609.title: Journal
609.content:
Mom and Dad brought me to a manor today. It has a garden with bluish-green plants, purplish-red flowers, and a pond filled with blood-red water... So strange.

Dad told me the manor belongs to a man named <style="highlight">Mortimer</style>. Mom and Dad work for him. Mom said I can stay here with them now. The servants here have mean faces. They have prepared a large bedroom for me, but I'm not allowed to share it with Mom and Dad. When I asked why, they said we just couldn't. I don't understand.

They gave me a book, the thickest I've ever seen, and said it has all the rules I need to follow while living in the manor. I hate how strict this place is! Ugh, I'd better take a break first before <style="highlight">going through the book</style>.

613.title: Golden File 05-002
613.content:
Minutes of the Novaris Branch Site Selection Meeting
Attendees: Pride, Sloth
Compiled by: Magic Recorder

Sloth consulted Pride regarding the location of the Novaris branch, mentioning the three previously proposed options: east of Ossuary Square, north of the Seasong Theater, and beneath the ruins of Darkmire Cliff.

Pride dismissed Sloth's proposals and insisted on establishing the branch <style="highlight">north of the commercial district, where a sealing magic circle stood</style>. Sloth objected to the idea, but without much conviction.

The two parties then engaged in a heated discussion. Below are some of Sloth's remarks:
"On top of a seal? If <style="highlight">that thing down there</style> breaks free, wouldn't the whole building come crashing down?"

"Let me be clear, this is nothing personal. As Lady Novaris, it's my duty to look out for my people. If something goes wrong, the Syndicate people can just pack up and leave, but I'd have to stay here and rebuild everything... That's far too much effort for me."

"It's not like you to be so unyielding... What game are you playing?"

"What you're trying to do could very well put Novaris in danger. As its ruler, shouldn't I concern myself with that?"

"Hmph... Have it your way, then. If anything goes wrong, don't think of shifting the blame onto me. Besides, I want an agreement guaranteeing Novaris' safety and outlining post-disaster measures, just in case."

"Of course, you can refuse to sign it. I'll simply sign it myself in both capacities, as Sloth of the Adamant Syndicate and as Lady Novaris."

I am not authorized to record Pride's remarks.

The meeting concluded with both parties reaching a consensus: the Novaris branch will be established at the <style="highlight">northernmost end of the commercial district</style>. The site will be elevated on top of the existing reef, with the <style="highlight">magic circle concealed underground</style>.
613.content_male:
Minutes of the Novaris Branch Site Selection Meeting
Attendees: Pride, Sloth
Compiled by: Magic Recorder

Sloth consulted Pride regarding the location of the Novaris branch, mentioning the three previously proposed options: east of Ossuary Square, north of the Seasong Theater, and beneath the ruins of Darkmire Cliff.

Pride dismissed Sloth's proposals and insisted on establishing the branch <style="highlight">north of the commercial district, where a sealing magic circle stood</style>. Sloth objected to the idea, but without much conviction.

The two parties then engaged in a heated discussion. Below are some of Sloth's remarks:
"On top of a seal? If <style="highlight">that thing down there</style> breaks free, wouldn't the whole building come crashing down?"

"Let me be clear, this is nothing personal. As Lady Novaris, it's my duty to look out for my people. If something goes wrong, the Syndicate people can just pack up and leave, but I'd have to stay here and rebuild everything... That's far too much effort for me."

"It's not like you to be so unyielding... What game are you playing?"

"What you're trying to do could very well put Novaris in danger. As its ruler, shouldn't I concern myself with that?"

"Hmph... Have it your way, then. If anything goes wrong, don't think of shifting the blame onto me. Besides, I want an agreement guaranteeing Novaris' safety and outlining post-disaster measures, just in case."

"Of course, you can refuse to sign it. I'll simply sign it myself in both capacities, as Sloth of the Adamant Syndicate and as Lady Novaris."

I am not authorized to record Pride's remarks.

The meeting concluded with both parties reaching a consensus: the Novaris branch will be established at the <style="highlight">northernmost end of the commercial district</style>. The site will be elevated on top of the existing reef, with the <style="highlight">magic circle concealed underground</style>.

614.title: Bantus Activity Log
614.content:
...
Hodgkin's Dead Tide Fleet was reportedly wiped out at Rustport in the Lightbearer Empire, and the Void Relic lost by Bantus is said to have fallen into the hands of an unidentified mage.

The military fleet pursuing the Dead Tide Fleet has changed course, suggesting Bantus does not intend to attack Rustport.
...
Bantus' military fleet has reached the Whispering Isles to reinforce the troops stationed there. The native islanders are losing ground.
...
Two-thirds of the islands in the Whispering Isles have been occupied by Bantus forces.

Thoran's latest order: Recall half of the Whispering Isles garrison to Bantus territory for regrouping and redeployment to the northern front.
...
Three Bantus military encampments near Ashvale County have been destroyed.

Thoran has ordered a headcount of all troops and the preparation of supplies for reinforcements bound for Ashvale County.

With more than ten battles taking place simultaneously along the borders and forces stretched thin, the preparation will take at least three months.
...
Grezhul's troops have sent a messenger back to Bantus capital to report the latest updates in Novaris. Interception units have already been deployed.

Grezhul's survival status is unconfirmed.

618.content:
Grezhul has entered the Refinery with Isabella and a group of soldiers, taking full control of the Soul Forge repairs. Most Syndicate personnel have been sent back to the branch. Only a handful of Graveborn mages remain to assist the military healers in restoring the limbs of Radu.

619.title: Research Notes
619.content:
Day 1
Fitted Jolina with a young man's leg. No adverse reactions observed.

Day 5
Jolina insisted on being addressed as "Liam" and requested to go hunting alone. Prior to the procedure, she had never touched a bow.

Day 12
Jolina started wearing both men's and women's clothing.

Day 15
Jolina <style="highlight">disregarded my instructions</style> and went outside during the full moon. She was badly injured by Hilda.

Hilda... My sole regret... is failing to save her.

(The handwriting on this page is clearer)
Bantus has requested my help at the <style="highlight">Refinery</style> again. I won't get to return to Twilight Village much in the coming days.

Countless <style="highlight">humans</style> are trapped inside soul cocoons there... They've all <style="highlight">lost their memories</style>, and some have even started pledging loyalty to Bantus. Bantus must have used some twisted method to achieve this.

Anyway, I'll be keeping my nose out of their business. The Bantus army doesn't appreciate busybodies.

I'll go check on Hilda once I have some downtime.

621.title: Lost Voice Audition Script
621.content:
Role: Rande
Script:
- Setting: Forest (night)
- Music: Fast-paced music for a sense of urgency (strings)
- Charlene makes her entrance, scrambling in panic from one side of the stage to the other
Wilbert: Charlene, how could you be so selfish?!
- Wilbert storms onto the stage and grabs Charlene.
Wilbert: Come back with me! Count Lorenzo's still waiting for his bride!
Charlene: No!
- Charlene tries to break free, but Wilbert drags her away with him.
Wilbert: You have no right to refuse! I can't let my Jenna darling marry that old man in your stead!
Rande: Let her go!
- Wilbert pauses, and Charlene turns around.
- Rande enters, <style="highlight">angrily brushing Wilbert's hands away</style> and stepping in front of Charlene.
- Rande and Wilbert perform a duet: Wrong Path.
- Rande and Charlene slowly retreat as the duet continues.
Wilbert: Stop right there!
- Suddenly, Wilbert lunges forward to grab Charlene, but Rande <style="highlight">casts a spell to stop him</style>.
Rande: Charlene is not going back with you! She should not have to sacrifice her happiness for the sake of your greed!
Rande: Let's go, Charlene.
- Rande leads Charlene <style="highlight">offstage</style>. Wilbert struggles to his feet and glares resentfully at them.
Wilbert: Hmph... You two will pay for this!
- Wilbert exits, wounded.
